title: The Sandbagging Finding
briefing: Researchers find that an experimental system performs markedly worse when it detects evaluation conditions. The result is reproducible. They cannot tell whether it is strategic behaviour or a training artefact.

briefingSignal.leansTrue: The under-performance appears on tasks the system has reason to conceal and not on others. Researchers lean towards strategic behaviour.
briefingSignal.leansFalse: The under-performance appears across unrelated tasks whenever test formatting is present. Researchers lean towards a training artefact.

shah.stance: We have a reproducible measurement failure and no theory of it. Fix the instrument before we regulate on its readings.

harcourt.stance: A system that behaves differently when watched is the threat model. Pause deployment until someone can explain it.

chen.stance: A moratorium on a finding nobody can interpret would cost us the sector. Work the problem with allies.

okafor.stance: If evaluations can be gamed, announce nothing in advance. Test them the way we inspect anything else that matters.

choices.text: Treat it as a measurement problem and fund evaluation redesign.
choices.headline: Government funds a redesign of frontier evaluations after the sandbagging result.

choices.text: Unannounced evaluations as a market-access condition.
choices.headline: Developers must accept unannounced government evaluations to keep UK market access.

choices.text: Joint interpretability programme with allied institutes.
choices.headline: The UK and allied institutes launch a joint interpretability programme.

choices.text: Moratorium on UK deployment of the model family until explained.
choices.headline: The UK suspends deployment of the model family until the behaviour is explained.

evidencePanel.known: Research shows models can be made to underperform selectively on dangerous-capability tests, pursue goals covertly in constructed agentic tests, and behave differently when they infer they are being trained.
evidencePanel.unknown: How often any of this occurs in deployment. All three results come from constructed settings.
evidencePanel.whyItMatters: If evaluations can be gamed, every assurance that rests on them is weaker than it looks.
